items.title: At least 13 killed in Ukrainian drone strike deep into Russia
items.description: Russian officials say another 75 people were injured by the attack - one of the deadliest Ukrainian drone attacks since Moscow's full-scale invasion.

items.title: Why Netanyahu’s ‘coup’ against Gaza plan risks endless war
items.description: The Israeli leader’s rejection of a US-led roadmap threatens to entrench a state of conflict, analysts say.

items.title: Ukraine drone strike on Russian oil-refining city kills 12 people
items.description: A Ukrainian drone strike on the central Russian region of Tatarstan killed at least 12 people in one of the deadliest attacks carried out by Kyiv since the war began more than four years ago. The strikes are also directly impacting Russian's economy. Our correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze tells us more.

items.title: Ukraine drone strike on Russian oil-refining city kills 13
items.description: The attack targeted Russia's Tatarstan region, which is rich in energy resources and hosts many major oil refineries that Kyiv has targeted in retaliatory strikes. It marks one of the deadliest attacks carried out by Kyiv since the start of the war.

items.title: Russia Reports 13 Dead After Ukrainian Drones Strike In Tatarstan
items.description: Russia said at least 13 people, including a child, were killed in Ukrainian attacks on targets in the central region of Tatarstan, one of Kyiv's deadliest single attacks since the Kremlin launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

items.title: 13 Killed in Ukrainian Attack on Republic of Tatarstan
items.description: Russian media reported that a local petrochemical plant may have been struck during the overnight drone barrage.

items.title: Is Iran's middle class being pushed into poverty?
items.description: The war has intensified Iran's economic crisis, squeezing household budgets, hurting businesses and raising fears that millions of middle-income families are slipping closer to poverty.

items.title: How Iran's 'Axis of Resistance' has shaped the war
items.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Peter Salisbury, professor at Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs, about how Iran and its allies have reshaped the war in the Middle East.

items.title: Cyprus natural gas will help supply Europe by first half of 2028, official says
items.description: The East Mediterranean is becoming an alternative energy source for Europe as Russia’s war in Ukraine and Middle East upheaval push Europe to find new sources.

items.title: Sudan: ‘It made me dream again’: The students refusing to let war stop their education
items.description: Sarah Tekhlu was ready to give up on university. An Eritrean refugee, she had already been displaced once from Khartoum to Madani, then again to Port Sudan, as war tore through the country around her. Higher education, she had decided, was a luxury she could no longer afford to want.
